current_answer: As of 15 October 2026, public evidence does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. OpenAI marked its 13 October GPT-6.1 Sol Codex/Work performance incident resolved at 16:36 UTC, but a Windows Pro Codex issue reports account-level capacity/503 errors across seven models through 14 October despite unused allowance, and a separate post-resolution issue reports GPT-6.1 Sol server_error for one saved reasoning item while controls complete. An older issue reports a similar saved-state failure before the status event. These are access or request-processing signals, not wrong completed answers or proof of broad model decline; their relationship and causes are unknown. Check current status, preserve the original task, record model/surface/client/context/error, and test a safe fresh task only when useful.

catalogue_card.question: Did Codex problems continue after OpenAI marked the incident resolved?
catalogue_card.text: One Windows user reports capacity errors across seven models after the status closure; another reports a GPT-6.1 Sol error tied to one saved history item. These are request failures, not proof of broad model decline.

summary: OpenAI marked the declared GPT-6.1 Sol Codex/Work performance event resolved on 13 October at 16:36 UTC; its status page does not show account-level recovery.

A Windows Pro Codex issue reports capacity/HTTP 503 errors across seven models despite unused allowance, through a 14 October snapshot. The author reports 88 capacity errors and 55 HTTP 503s; one request was said to be confirmed server-overload by Support.
A separate post-resolution diagnostic reports one GPT-6.1 Sol saved reasoning item failing before output while same-model and GPT-6 Sol controls completed.
An earlier Codex issue reports a similar saved-reasoning failure before the 13 October status event. Shared cause is unknown.
Neither capacity errors nor no-output request failures measure completed-answer quality. No broad multi-provider matched before/after series establishes capability decline.
Check status, preserve the original history, record the surface and exact error, and test a safe fresh task only when useful.
uncertainty: OpenAI's status resolution is aggregate and does not establish each account's recovery.
The capacity logs are a single account's reported data, with no follow-up checked after 14 October 08:23 UTC.
The similar saved-history reports are user-defined tests with small samples; provider-side correlation and common cause are absent.
No multi-provider matched before-and-after task series establishes broad capability decline.
Analytics were unavailable; reader use, repeat visits, actions and revenue remain unknown, not zero.
